issues.description: Guard condition lacks a stated invariant for which keys should accept completions.
issues.detail: The new branch fires when use_enter_for_completions is False and key != Tab, but this block executes inside a handler whose entry conditions (Enter/Return/Tab/Shift+Tab?) are not visible in the diff. Without a comment naming the precondition ("key is Enter or Return"), a future reader cannot prove the branch only suppresses Enter and not, say, an arrow key. Name the invariant or narrow the test to explicit Key_Return/Key_Enter.

issues.description: Negated equality comparison reads awkwardly and obscures intent.
issues.detail: `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` parses as `not (key == Qt.Key_Tab)` by Python precedence, which is correct but reads as a stumble. Prefer `key != Qt.Key_Tab`. Small readability cost, but this is precisely the literate-programming surface where a careful reader pauses and re-checks precedence rather than reading the algorithm.

issues.description: Tab-only fallback ignores Shift+Tab and platform Enter variants without comment.
issues.detail: The condition treats Qt.Key_Tab as the sole accept key when Enter is disabled. Qt distinguishes Key_Enter (numpad) from Key_Return, and Shift+Tab is conventionally back-tab. The code is likely correct because the outer handler filters keys, but the postcondition ("Tab accepts; everything else dismisses and forwards") should be stated in a one-line comment so the reader does not have to reconstruct it.

issues.description: Config read on every keystroke instead of cached at popup show.
issues.detail: self.get_conf(...) runs on every keyPressEvent while the completion popup is visible. The cost is small but nonzero, and the value cannot change mid-keystroke. Hoisting the lookup to popup-show time (or caching on a config-changed signal) is the textbook move; leaving it inline is fine if measured, but no measurement is presented. ASYMPTOTICALLY-OK-PRACTICALLY-FINE, flagged only for the record.

issues.description: No test exercising the new branch is included.
issues.detail: Per the lens: proofs catch what tests miss, tests catch what proofs miss. The new option introduces a second control-flow path through keyPressEvent. A small unit or integration test toggling use_enter_for_completions and asserting that Enter dismisses-and-forwards while Tab still accepts would close the loop. "Tried correct" beats "only argued correct."

review.summary: Verdict: UNDER-AUDITED / NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT. The change is small and the algorithm is straightforward: when Enter-to-accept is disabled and the pressed key is not Tab, hide the popup and forward the event. The functional logic is plausibly correct, but the diff leaves the precondition of the surrounding handler implicit, uses `not key == X` where `key != X` would read more cleanly, and ships no test for the new branch. None of these are blockers; one comment naming the invariant and a single test toggling the option would move this from "tried correct" to "argued correct."
